rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header (§4's sibling).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule-drift re-check (compendium `modified: 2026-08-25`, after pin b55cd28b — see drift_rules_reread). Re-fetched current wording via `node curriculum/evals/scripts/rule.js lectures 5`: 'Enforced by scripts/check-slide-size.js (--report = distribution largest-first; default gate exits 1 on any oversized; --file for one file...)'. Ran the enforcer directly against this file: `node ./scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md --report` → 8 slides measured, 1 flagged oversized ('Three paths to a work-app action', 211w/3b, 1 word over the 210w bar). On its own this reads as a REVISE-worthy hit. But the SAME script's own header comment states the design intent explicitly: 'The file set is derived, not hand-listed: each AE101 module's exercises/<slug> and lectures/<slug> includes... reference and supplementary pages sit outside it' — confirmed by running the script's default corpus scan with no --file flag: `node ./scripts/check-slide-size.js --report` enumerates only lecture/exercise slides and never lists this file. --file is a stated on-demand measurement affordance for any path, not evidence the mechanical gate covers reference pages. This is corroborated by two independent sources: curriculum/quality-format.md § Key rules ('Reference files (curriculum/trainings/<training>/reference/) exempt — flat lookup, no mood / sim surface') and .claude/rules/content-rules.md's slide-rendered-surface definition, which enumerates 'AE101 lectures/exercises/modules' as the covered set for slide-chunking rules and does not name reference. Verdict stands at N/A: the rule's own enforcement mechanism and two independent canon docs agree reference pages are out of its scope, by design, not by oversight. The 1-word-over near-miss is logged as a non-blocking TODO in case the maintainer ever widens the gate.
